messages:
alice: Anyone seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal.model.prod from pods on GPU nodes after batch-proxy rollout? Started after we enabled batch-proxy on gpu-pool-3.
ben: Yep, alerts started around 2026-03-14T02:00Z. Only name resolution fails; IP egress works. Affects eu-west-prod and us-east-staging.
carmen: Stack: pod -> node-local-dns (CoreDNS forward) -> host systemd-resolved(127.0.0.53) -> on-prem forwarder -> Route53. Forwarder logs show short windows of SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN during high fanout.
alice: Repro: inside gpu pod getaddrinfo("internal.model.prod") returns EAI_NONAME intermittently under load. strace indicates we receive a UDP reply with TC set but pod never follows up with a TCP retry.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout batch-proxy v2 to gpu-pool-3 completed at 2026-03-14T12:12:08Z :information_source:
dave: My hunch: conntrack / NAT port exhaustion because batch-proxy creates many simultaneous outbound connections. But tcpdump shows truncated UDP responses (TC=1) and no TCP SYNs from pods toward upstream.
elaine: systemd-resolved behaves like a stub resolver and historically hasn't always initiated TCP fallback for EDNS-truncated replies. Our node-local CoreDNS expects the host stub to do TCP fallback.
ben: Captured on node: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 53` -> DNS response with TC flag, then pod keeps issuing UDP queries. No outbound TCP to forwarder observed. If firewall/NAT blocks outbound TCP to forwarder, fallback won't work.
alice: Minimal repro (flaky):
```
# inside gpu pod
$ dig +bufsize=4096 internal.model.prod @127.0.0.53
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, flags: qr tc ; Truncated
# no subsequent tcp attempt observed
```
carmen: Also note split-horizon upstream: on-prem forwarder sometimes returns NXDOMAIN briefly during its own failover, which negative caches into node-local/CoreDNS and causes downstream failures for the TTL.
elaine: Short-term mitigations to try:
- reduce EDNS UDP buffer on forwarders or CoreDNS (e.g., edns0 size=1232)
- force TCP for DNS between node-local and forwarder or allow DNS-over-TCP unblocked
- lower negative caching ttl on forwarder or upstream
- increase conntrack table and reduce UDP timeout on GPU nodes

dave: Conntrack proposals:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout=30
```
Also check iptables/fgw rules for dropped fragments; EDNS+large UDP replies may fragment on path.
ben: I'll open INF ticket and attach packet captures, dig outputs, affected pod names (gpu-scaler-7f5, tuner-2b4, embedder-11c). Short-term routing: point node-local on GPU nodes at secondary forwarder that accepts TCP.
infra-bot: ticket INF-4321 created: "DNS TCP fallback + batch-proxy NXDOMAIN" priority=P1
carmen: I'll prototype `forward . 10.20.30.40:53 { edns0 1232 }` on one gpu node and run a load generator to validate.
ben: If that stabilizes, we can roll config cluster-wide and add a DNS e2e smoke check tied to batch-proxy rollouts to prevent future regressions.
elaine: Fyi, saw similar behavior before where systemd-resolved swallowed TCP fallback when upstream IPs changed quickly; split-horizon TTLs can make this worse.
alice: Pausing further batch-proxy rollouts for gpu pool until we have a mitigation plan. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
